robot.name: Booster T1
robot.status_notes: Booster's current site features T2 and K1; T1 remains available through authorized distributors and resellers, including used units. No direct Booster sale or new production confirmed.

height.original_value: 1.18 m (118 cm); some sources say ~1.2 m
height.notes: Source 6 archived Booster spec lists 118 × 47 × 23 cm; source 2 says 1.18 m; sources 1, 5, 7 say ~1.2 m. Use 118 cm.

payload.notes: Rated payload is per arm, roughly a full water bottle. No total payload published.

runtime.notes: Standing runtime is about 4 hours; walking runtime is best-case.

battery.original_value: 10.5 Ah swappable battery (reseller); 9.5 Ah swappable per Humanoza
battery.notes: Source 4 lists 10.5 Ah replacement battery for T1; source 6 table says 10.5 Ah; source 2 says 9.5 Ah swappable with 10.5 Ah charging setup. Conflict noted.

walking_speed.original_value: roughly 0.97 m/s walking (source 2); no official walking speed published per source 5
walking_speed.notes: Humanoza calls it a published maximum for stable omnidirectional walking, not a sustained cruise. Humanoid Press says no official walking speed published. Use with caution.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Standard 23 DoF (6 per leg, 4 per arm, 1 waist, 2 head); 31 with grippers (7-DoF arms), 41 with dexterous hands.

hands.description: Base configuration has simple end effectors/stubs and no manipulation. Optional grippers (31 DoF total) or dexterous hands (41 DoF total) available.

items: depth/RGB-D camera (Intel depth camera per source 2)
3D LiDAR (source 2 only; not in official spec table)

compute.description: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 32 GB (~200 TOPS) standard; Standard/Customized versions add Intel Core i7-1370P. Basic version may only have Jetson.

actuators.description: Full force-controlled actuators with dual encoders; mixed torque/velocity/position control; knee joint peak torque 130 N·m.

availability.notes: Available through authorized distributors and resellers; Booster does not publish MSRP. US reseller prices: Basic ~$29,800, Standard ~$33,949, with grippers ~$50,925. EU used unit listed at €31,200. No official price.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: T1 is locomotion-first; base arms are 4-DoF with no hands. Optional grippers (31 DoF) or dexterous hands (41 DoF) enable basic grasping/fine manipulation, payload ~0.5 kg per arm. No detailed manipulation demo or success rate found.
caveats: No manipulation video transcript or independent benchmark
No grip force or hand DoF specification
Payload is very low; not for physical work

autonomy_task_execution.summary: Supports onboard learned policies, teleoperation, and autonomous RoboCup play via official robocup_demo. RoboCup matches are unscripted but autonomy details not documented in reviewed sources. Source 2 says realistic deployment has a person near kill switch; not unattended.
caveats: Autonomy not independently verified
Teleoperation_status for videos not disclosed
No intervention logs

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Omnidirectional walking at ~0.97 m/s, push/fall recovery, rising from prone, dynamic motions; 2025 RoboCup AdultSize champion and 2026 Large division title; official video titles indicate CES unstoppable and soccer solution, but content not reviewed.
caveats: Video content not reviewed; titles only
No official walking speed or fall-recovery metric published per Humanoid Press
Speed figure is best-case

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Depth camera, 9-axis IMU, mic array/speaker, optional LiDAR? Compute 200 TOPS enables onboard vision models. No specific perception benchmark or demo described.
caveats: Sensor list inconsistent and not fully official
No camera resolution/LiDAR type published
Perception capability inferred from hardware only

human_interaction.summary: Microphone array and speaker support ASR/TTS, mobile app control; designed for HRI experiments. No demo evidence found.
caveats: No speech recognition accuracy or user study

endurance_reliability.summary: Quoted ~2 h walking, ~4 h standing on swappable battery; RoboCup competition format exposes fall recovery and thermal endurance, but no official endurance test or failure data. Source 6 notes need padded floor, emergency stop.
caveats: Runtime best-case
No independent reliability data
No IP rating/operating temp

human_environment_fit.summary: 1.18 m, 30 kg, two-person carry; designed for flat indoor lab/classroom/competition surfaces; not outdoors/uneven terrain; source 6 warns padded floor and safety gantry.
caveats: No safety certification
Falls on hard floor damage robot and may injure people

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: Sold through authorized distributors; Booster says >50 teams/institutions adopted; named university users include Purdue, Carnegie Mellon, UC Berkeley (from archived Booster page); RoboCup wins with Tsinghua team.
caveats: No customer press releases or deployment metrics
Names from reseller guide citing archived page
No unit sales volume officially confirmed

accessibility_value.summary: Purchasable via resellers with configurations from ~$29,800 Basic to ~$50,925 with grippers in US; EU used unit €31,200. Booster publishes no MSRP, and pricing varies by region/config.
caveats: No official price list
US import may be restricted by FCC after July 2026, authorization unclear
Prices are reseller quotes and change

evidence_items.title: Booster T1 research/education positioning
evidence_items.claim: Booster T1 is a full-body bipedal humanoid sold as a developer platform to universities, research institutes and competition teams; it is a research and education platform, not a competitor to Figure or Optimus.
evidence_items.notes: Humanoza editorial review, verified against maker docs.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The T1 is a full-body bipedal humanoid built by Booster Robotics, a Beijing company founded in 2023, and sold as a developer platform to universities, research institutes and competition teams.
evidence_items.source_location: Humanoza article, What is the Booster T1 Robot? section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Media summary; consistent with reseller product pages.

evidence_items.title: Height, weight, payload, speed
evidence_items.claim: T1 stands 1.18 m, weighs ~30 kg, walks at ~0.97 m/s, payload ~0.5 kg per arm.
evidence_items.notes: Humanoza values; source 6 confirms 118cm, 30kg, speed not published.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Defines size, speed and manipulation limits.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: It stands 1.18 m, weighs about 30 kg, walks omnidirectionally at roughly 0.97 m/s - call it 3.5 km/h, a slow human stroll - and carries a payload of about 0.5 kg per arm.
evidence_items.source_location: Humanoza article, What is the Booster T1 paragraph
evidence_items.verification_notes: Speed not official per Humanoid Press; payload is per arm low.

evidence_items.title: Degrees of freedom configurations
evidence_items.claim: Base 23 DoF, 31 with grippers, 41 with dexterous hands.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Shows modularity but base lacks hands.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The base machine has 23 degrees of freedom. Fit the optional grippers and that becomes 31; fit the dexterous hands and it becomes 41.
evidence_items.source_location: Humanoza article, What is the Booster T1 section

evidence_items.title: Onboard compute specification
evidence_items.claim: Standard configuration has NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 32 GB (~200 TOPS) plus Intel Core i7-1370P.
evidence_items.notes: Source 6 says Basic may only have AGX Orin; Standard/Customized add Intel.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: On the Standard configuration the compute is genuinely serious for the size class - an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin with 32 GB, quoted at around 200 TOPS, alongside an Intel Core i7-1370P.
evidence_items.source_location: Humanoza article, What is the Booster T1 section

evidence_items.title: Sensor suite claim
evidence_items.claim: Depth/RGB-D camera, 3D LiDAR, 9-axis IMU, joint encoders, six-microphone array and speaker.
evidence_items.notes: LiDAR not in official table source 6; use cautiously.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Sensing covers an Intel depth/RGB-D camera, a 3D LiDAR, a nine-axis IMU, joint encoders throughout, and a six-microphone array with speaker for voice work.
evidence_items.source_location: Humanoza article, What is the Booster T1 section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Source 5 says full sensor list not published; source 6 only lists depth camera, 9-axis IMU, 6-mic array speaker.

evidence_items.title: Battery and runtime
evidence_items.claim: Battery 9.5 Ah swappable, quoted endurance about two hours walking and four hours standing.
evidence_items.notes: Source 4/6 list 10.5 Ah battery; conflict noted.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Battery: 9.5 Ah, swappable, with a 10.5 Ah charging setup. Quoted endurance is about two hours walking and about four hours standing.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Runtime best-case per source 2; walking heavily dependent on gait.

evidence_items.title: US reseller pricing and availability
evidence_items.claim: As of 30 Aug 2026, US distributor pricing: Basic ~$29,800, Standard ~$33,949, Standard with grippers ~$50,925.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: As of 30 August 2026, authorised distributor pricing in the US looks like this: about $29,800 for the T1 Basic, about $33,949 for the T1 Standard, and about $50,925 for a Standard with grippers.
evidence_items.source_location: Humanoza article, How much does a Booster T1 cost? section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Prices from reseller quote sheets; move and exclude shipping/customs.

evidence_items.title: RoboCup championships
evidence_items.claim: T1 took AdultSize title at RoboCup 2025 with Tsinghua Hephaestus, and Large division at RoboCup 2026; THU Huoshen Team retained title with back-to-back championships.
evidence_items.notes: Independent competition outcome reported by media.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: At RoboCup 2025 it took the AdultSize title under Tsinghua University's Hephaestus team, and at RoboCup 2026 in South Korea it did it again in the Large division - while Booster's smaller K1 took the Middle division under Germany's B-Human and a K1 Air took the Small.
evidence_items.source_location: Humanoza article, Overview section; Interesting Engineering article
evidence_items.verification_notes: RoboCup is independent, but details of autonomy and hardware modifications not provided.

evidence_items.title: Open software/SDK/ROS2
evidence_items.claim: T1 supports ROS 2, open SDK, high/low APIs, simulation tools Isaac Sim, MuJoCo, Webots; open-source training code on GitHub.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The T1’s software environment is fully open and developer-friendly, supporting ROS 2, an open SDK, high- and low-level APIs and compatibility with major simulation tools like Isaac Sim and MuJoCo.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Source 6 confirms SDK, ROS2 interface, booster_gym public.

evidence_items.title: Named university adopters
evidence_items.claim: Booster lists university users: Purdue table-tennis project, CMU FALCON RL framework, UC Berkeley FastTD3 algorithm.
evidence_items.notes: From archived Booster page via Robotics Center guide.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Booster lists university users of the T1 on its archived page, including a table-tennis project at Purdue, the FALCON RL framework at Carnegie Mellon and the FastTD3 algorithm at UC Berkeley.
evidence_items.source_location: Robotics Center guide, Which Booster should you buy? section

evidence_items.title: Missing sensor specs
evidence_items.claim: Booster Robotics confirms advanced sensing but does not publish a full sensor list.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Booster Robotics confirms advanced sensing but does not publish a full sensor list.
evidence_items.source_location: Humanoid Press database, Perception & Sensors section

evidence_items.title: Walking speed not officially published
evidence_items.claim: No official walking speed, step height, incline capability, or fall-recovery metrics have been published.
evidence_items.notes: Humanoid Press notes official gap; source 2 provides 0.97 m/s but not official.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: No official walking speed, step height, incline capability, or fall-recovery metrics have been published.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Source 2 media gives 0.97 m/s, but not from Booster official.

evidence_items.title: US import authorization unclear
evidence_items.claim: US buyers: no pre-July 2026 FCC authorization for T1 appears in public records; ask distributor for FCC ID.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: US buyers: no pre-July 2026 authorization for the T1 is on public record — ask your distributor for the FCC ID.
evidence_items.source_location: Humanoza article, Buying the Booster T1 — Status unclear section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Source 6 also mentions FCC Covered List; new models may not receive authorization.

evidence_items.title: Limits: payload and supervision
evidence_items.claim: The T1 is a research and education platform, comparing it to Figure 03, Apollo or Tesla Optimus is a category error; rated payload about 0.5 kg per arm; not for physical work.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The T1 is a research and education platform, and comparing it to Figure 03, Apollo or Tesla Optimus is a category error.
evidence_items.source_location: Humanoza article, What it actually does section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Consistent with payload spec and reseller positioning.

evidence_items.claim: Booster has not published walking speed, payload, grip force, camera resolution, IP rating, etc.
evidence_items.notes: Humanoid Press list of not published specs.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: T1 is purchasable through resellers and authorized distributors, but Booster publishes no MSRP. US import authorization after July 2026 FCC changes is unclear; buyers are advised to verify FCC ID.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Accessibility/value should reflect reseller-only availability and possible US import restrictions.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: Base T1 has no hands and 4-DoF arms; payload is only ~0.5 kg per arm. Gripper and dexterous hand versions exist but are expensive.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Manipulation scores should be low for base configuration; treatment as a manipulation robot is a category error.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: Source 2 describes teleop + onboard AI and says realistic deployment has a person near kill switch. Video titles provide no autonomy disclosure.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Do not credit autonomous task execution beyond the RoboCup competition context, and avoid strong autonomy claims.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: No official walking speed, step height, incline, fall-recovery metrics, payload, grip force, camera resolution, LiDAR type, IP rating, or full sensor list are published by Booster.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Many spec-based dimensions remain evidence_level 1 or 0; avoid filling gaps from third-party directories.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: RoboCup wins are independent but do not provide per-robot reliability metrics, intervention counts, or autonomy logs. Winning team may modify hardware/software.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Credit dynamic mobility and fall recovery but not general autonomous deployment.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: All provided video sources have only titles; no transcripts or content descriptions were available. Therefore no capabilities from videos can be credited.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Mobility and autonomy evidence from demos should be considered unverified until manual review.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: Booster T1 is a compact (1.18 m, 30 kg) bipedal research humanoid with open SDK, ROS 2, strong onboard compute (Jetson AGX Orin + i7), and a genuine RoboCup competition record (2025 AdultSize champion, 2026 Large division). However, it is not an industrial or home robot: base has no hands, payload is ~0.5 kg per arm, many specifications are unpublished by Booster, and it has been superseded on Booster's own site by T2/K1.
strongest_positive_evidence: 2025 RoboCup AdultSize champion under Tsinghua Hephaestus.
2026 RoboCup Large division title / back-to-back championships reported by Interesting Engineering.
Available through multiple resellers with detailed US/EU pricing; open-source SDK and ROS2 support.
Named academic adopters: Purdue table-tennis, CMU FALCON RL, UC Berkeley FastTD3.
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No official walking speed, step height, incline, fall-recovery metrics.
No full sensor list, camera resolution, LiDAR type, IP rating.
No payload or grip force officially published.
Video evidence only titles; no transcript or content review.
No autonomy logs or unattended operation evidence.
conflicting_claims: Height: 1.18 m (Humanoza) vs ~1.2 m (multiple resellers/Humanoid Press).
Battery capacity: 9.5 Ah (Humanoza) vs 10.5 Ah (Generation Robots battery listing, Robotics Center table).
Walking speed: ~0.97 m/s (Humanoza) vs 'not published' (Humanoid Press/Robotics Center table).
Price: US Basic $29,800 vs EU used €31,200 vs Muzix ex-VAT €33,099; all reseller figures, no MSRP.
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit industrial or warehouse manipulation; payload is ~0.5 kg per arm and base has no hands.
Do not treat 0.97 m/s as an official Booster spec.
Do not credit autonomy from video titles; no transcripts were available.
Do not treat RoboCup wins as evidence of commercial deployment or general autonomous task execution outside competition.
Do not claim T1 is current on Booster's site; it has been superseded by T2/K1 although still sold by resellers.
Do not use the provided K1 video (source 13) for T1 evidence.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: Booster T1 is a 1.18 m, 30 kg bipedal research humanoid from Booster Robotics with 23 DoF standard (31 grippers, 41 dexterous hands), NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin compute, ROS 2 SDK, and ~2 h walking runtime. Strongest evidence is RoboCup success: 2025 AdultSize champion and 2026 Large division title. It is purchasable through resellers (~$29,800-$50,925) but Booster publishes no MSRP; payload is only ~0.5 kg per arm, base has no hands, and many specs (walking speed, full sensor list) are not officially published. It is a research/education platform, now superseded by T2/K1 on Booster's site.
strongest_evidence: 2025 RoboCup AdultSize champion and 2026 Large division title (evidence_008).
US reseller pricing and availability with open software/SDK (evidence_007, evidence_009).
Named university adopters from archived Booster page (evidence_010).
weakest_evidence: No official walking speed or fall-recovery metrics published (evidence_012).
No full sensor list or manipulation payload/grip force (evidence_011, evidence_015).
All video sources are titles only; no content reviewed (demos).
known_do_not_credit: Single MSRP or direct Booster sale
Source 13 (Booster K1 video) for T1 evidence
